clauses.reason: The sole paragraph of Executive Order 8341 says that Executive Order No. 8323 of January 22, 1940 "is hereby revoked." It is a present-tense, self-executing revocation with no deferred effective date, condition or continuing duty, so the command was performed and ended when the order was signed on February 8, 1940, the date printed in the held text. The filing date (February 9, 1940) and the issue date (February 10, 1940) are alternative readings, and none moves the end outside February 1940. The revocation of Executive Order No. 8323 remains as a surviving effect of the completed act. No held instrument revokes, amends or extends Executive Order 8341.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 8341 of February 8, 1940 (5 FR 643, Federal Register issue of Saturday, February 10, 1940; FR Doc. 40-606, filed February 9, 1940) is a single paragraph. Its only operative act is to revoke Executive Order No. 8323 of January 22, 1940, which had abolished Customs Collection District No. 43 (Tennessee), revoked the designations of Memphis, Chattanooga and Nashville as customs ports of entry, and extended the limits of Customs Collection District No. 42 (Kentucky) and Customs Collection District No. 45 (St. Louis). The held text says the earlier order "is hereby revoked." The paragraph states no later effective date, condition, report or continuing duty, so by its own terms the act was performed, and the command exhausted, when the order was signed on February 8, 1940. Identity rests on the heading, the signing date, the Federal Register document line and the page; the machine-extracted text prints the closing order-number line with a stray character and omits the number from the heading, which the packet records as a segmentation lead. The working text is the official Federal Register page text extracted from the PDF by OCR, not an authenticated transcription; page images were not inspected.

savings.reason: The revocation of Executive Order No. 8323 was carried out when Executive Order 8341 was signed on February 8, 1940. That result is a surviving effect of a completed act and is not a command that Executive Order 8341 continues to impose. The held text has no savings clause, exception or pending proceeding, and no held source shows any right or duty left outstanding by it.
